title: Course Schedule
description: Cycle detection on a directed graph via Kahn topological sort: peel zero-indegree nodes until none remain. If all peeled, no cycle.

notes: Kahn BFS produces a topological order as a side effect and uses no recursion stack.
Pair [a, b] means "take b before a" — edge b -> a in the prerequisite-to-course direction.
If `taken < numCourses` at the end, the remainder contains a cycle.

questions.q: Course Schedule reduces to which classic graph question?
options: Cycle detection in a directed graph

questions.q: In Kahn algorithm, which nodes go into the queue initially?
options: Nodes with zero indegree (no remaining prerequisites)

questions.q: How do you conclude that a cycle exists?
options: The queue runs out before all nodes are taken
The graph has more edges than nodes
A node appears in the queue twice

exercises.prompt: Fill in Kahn BFS topological sort.

blanks.hint: every edge into a bumps its indegree
seed the queue with nodes having no prerequisites
one prerequisite of n is now satisfied
strict equality — peeled every node iff acyclic

L3.prompt: Write `canFinish(numCourses, prerequisites)` returning true iff all courses can be taken. Pair `[a, b]` means take b before a. Log `canFinish(2, [[1, 0]])` then `canFinish(2, [[1, 0], [0, 1]])`.
hints: Build adjacency + indegree arrays from pairs.
Kahn BFS: queue zero-indegree, decrement on dequeue, count peeled.
